_readme: Single source of truth for the validation POLICY PARAMETERS the hub (backend/util/validate, internal/worker/gitutil) and the browser (frontend/src/lib/validate.ts) both enforce: byte limits, the character classes a title loses or folds, the session-ID refusals, the password limits, and the git branch-name rules. The ALGORITHMS stay hand-written per language (each side's scanner, trim, and error wording are its own); testdata/*_conformance.json remains the behavioral differential between them. What this file kills is the hand-copied parameter set: a class edited here regenerates both sides' tables, and the conformance fixtures prove the algorithms still agree. Code points are decimal; each range is a [lo, hi, name] triple identifying its character(s) -- the generator emits the name as a trailing comment in the Go tables and ignores it on the TS side (a regex class has nowhere to put it), and the name is required so no entry ships as a bare number pair. session.byteLimit caps a resume handle that is a TOKEN; session.filePathByteLimit caps one that is a session FILE PATH (Pi's shape), because a path is longer than a token by construction and the token cap refused every real one. The generator refuses a file-path cap that is not larger. session.invisibleFormat repeats name.invisibleFormat on purpose: the session rule is FROZEN, so a later change to what a NAME may hold cannot move what a TOKEN may hold. The generator enforces the repetition -- edit one list and generation fails until a human decides both move.
